How a load runs — start to sealed

The whole chain, the way the newest build runs it — try every step live on the Loads and Money tabs with the fake RUGGS fleet:

🚪 Broker sends→ 🖥️ Desk accepts→ 🧑‍✈️ Driver assigned→ 🚛 Driver runs it→ 🔗 Receiver confirms on the link→ ⛓️ Delivery seals itself→ 🗄️ Lands in the Library — printable, emailable, downloadable

Fleet owners — your desk books it, your drivers run it, the record seals itself. One Desk and the boards are on the Loads tab; the Library — every record in one home — is on the Money tab.

A perfect day pays exactly 500 points, plus a +200 clean-week streak bonus. Points convert at $0.25 per 1,000 SM Points, paid in $STONER at the live price at payout, with a minimum conversion of 10,000 points (10,000 points = $2.50 worth of $STONER). Conversions open at launch — November 20, 2026 — for paying tiers, so until then this shows an honest “opens at launch” state. On Basic (free), sealed trips and on-time PODs earn half — 60 and 82 points — and there are no fuel-stop points, since fuel routes and the planner are paid-tier. Your points are yours — they never expire, and staying on the free tier never costs you your balance: free-tier points are never forfeited for staying free and never wiped by any season reset, and a free driver keeps and stacks his full balance, but he cannot convert while free — converting unlocks only when he upgrades to a paying tier; on upgrade the retained balance converts under the normal rules (10,000-point minimum). Full points panel on the Money tab.

Hill grade alerts (sample)

Scripted into the demo drive above — press START GPS and the calls play in order on this sample route. The alert banner carries your live demo speed, and while you're on a grade the small readout sits beside the speed bubble on the map — ▼ 6% going down, ▲ 5% climbing. Turn them off any time in Settings → Driving → Hill grade alerts.

⚠️
Downgrade — 6% for 1.2 miles ahead
Called half a mile out, with your live speed on the banner. Gear down · check your brakes before the crest.
⛰️
At the crest — downgrade starts now
The second call, at the top: 6% for 1.2 mi. Gear down now — ride the engine brake and save the service brakes for when you need them.
⬆️
Climb — 5% for 2.0 miles ahead
Called half a mile out. Loaded, you'll lose speed on the climb — pick your lane early and let the truck pull.

Speed-limit sign — always labelled (sample)

The speed-limit sign always says what it knows — posted limit, last known, checking, or no data — and never just goes blank at a bare “––”. Press START GPS above and watch it work through the states on this sample run; the same captions ride the Cab display sign.

…
CHECKING… — lookup in flight
The drive opens with the sign briefly reading CHECKING… while the limit lookup runs, instead of sitting unexplained and blank.
65
Posted limit — the number, captioned
Once the lookup lands, the sign settles to the posted limit — 65 on this sample run — labelled POSTED LIMIT.
↺
LAST KNOWN LIMIT — held, not blanked
Later in the drive the lookup runs slow for a stretch, and the sign holds the last posted 65 labelled LAST KNOWN LIMIT rather than dropping to a blank.
—
NO LIMIT DATA — the parked settle
Stop the demo drive and park, and the sign settles to NO LIMIT DATA with its caption — it doesn't spin and it doesn't sit blank.

Crossings on your route, called ahead — ease up, look both ways, stop clear of the tracks.

Android Auto & Cab Mode (preview)

📺

Head-unit projection is not live yet — it arrives with the Play Store release. Try Cab Mode on the phone and the three template previews below. Nothing in this preview connects to a real vehicle.

What is Cab Mode? Cab Mode puts STONEMILES on the truck's own screen — the head unit — instead of a phone swinging on a mount. It is built for hotshots, commercial rigs and fleet trucks, and the new 2027 cabs & semis: a dually's factory dash running Android Auto, or the big factory screens landing in 2027 Peterbilt and Kenworth cabs and semis. Cab Mode fills that screen with what a load actually needs — your next turn big enough to read at a glance, your speed against the posted limit, ETA and miles left, your drive clock, truck stops, parking and weigh stations ahead, and road alerts that matter when you are hauling. No squinting, no reaching for the phone — eyes up, hands on the wheel, load moving. And nothing else in the cab does this: no other screen carries the load with it — the drive clock tied to your sealed trip, what to expect at the dock when you arrive, and a green route line at night. Basic includes the basic cab display; Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner include the full version. No separate price — it is part of the tier.

Cab Mode is included by tier — it is never sold separately and has no price of its own. Basic gets the basic version: the glanceable Guidance screen. Gold, Diamond, and Fleet / Owner get the full version, which adds auto-open with guidance, voice directions on the cab display, the HOS tile, and the Stops ahead + Road alerts screens. stonemiles.app/receive/1042-DEMO

The QR prints right on the BOL and the link rides with it. The receiver opens it on their own phone — no app, no account — checks the freight, notes any damage or shortage, and confirms. That confirmation is the POD.

THREE DOORS AT THE DOCK — THE FIRST ONE USED SEALS IT

Docks sign three ways, and all three feed the same sealed record. Whichever door gets used first closes the delivery — the other two just show “already confirmed,” never a double entry.

Receive link: the receiver opens the link (or scans the QR), confirms the freight on their own phone, and signs with a fingertip. Fill the receiver side in below — in the full app this is the receiver's own screen.

Sign on the driver's phone: no link needed — the receiver signs right here on the driver's screen, name under it, any damage or shortage noted on the spot. That signature becomes the sealed POD.

Paper BOL: the driver prints the BOL (QR rides on it), the receiver signs the paper, and the driver photographs the signed BOL and uploads it as the POD. The paper is the signature; the photo seals it.

How sealing works

Every trip, load, and delivery gets a fingerprint (a SHA-256 hash) chained to the record before it. Change any old record and every fingerprint after it breaks — so a sealed sheet proves it wasn't quietly edited. On-chain anchoring stays off until a separate go-live call.

Verify & Audit — proof lookup (sample)

Verify & Audit proof lookup: every sealed record carries a QR and a short code. A broker, receiver, or auditor can look up the proof and check a record is genuine without an account — the code either matches the hash chain or it doesn't.

CONVERSION — OPENS AT LAUNCH
Conversion rate$0.25 per 1,000 SM Points

StatusOpens at launch
OpensNovember 20, 2026 — at launch

Points are earned only from GPS-verified events — for sealed work. They are not a token and are never sendable or tradable — conversion by the driver who earned them is the one exit, and conversion opens at the Nov 20 launch for paying tiers; for a free/Basic account it additionally unlocks only on upgrade to a paying tier. Until then no conversion can be made from this panel. Points keep earning in the meantime. This rate is a conversion rate, not a promise of earnings. On Basic (free), sealed trips and on-time PODs earn half points — 60 and 82 — and fuel-stop points aren't earned: fuel routes and the planner are paid-tier features. Your points are yours — they never expire, and staying on the free tier never costs you your balance: free-tier points are never forfeited for staying free and never wiped by any season reset, and a free driver keeps and stacks his full balance, but he cannot convert while free — converting unlocks only when he upgrades to a paying tier; on upgrade the retained balance converts under the normal rules (10,000-point minimum). If a paying account lapses for non-renewal and is later reactivated, conversion and cash-out stay held for 2 weeks from reactivation — sample: “Reactivated — your balance unlocks on November 9, 2026 while your account stays active” — and cancelling during the hold starts a fresh 2-week retainer.

Security Pack 2

🔐Account-takeover protection — authenticator 2FA for Owner & Dispatch, new-device sign-in alerts, an active-sessions screen, and sign-out-everywhere.
🚪Sign out, right up top — the Sign out button sits in the top bar beside the menu, and one confirm tap signs out this device. After signing out, only a real credential gets you back in — app PIN, Face ID / fingerprint, or the full sign-in under “Sign in with a different account.” There is no one-tap back-in.
📵Lost-phone kill switch — remote session kill and lock from any signed-in device; a fresh PIN is required before wallet, EIN, settlements, or exports open.
⛓Sealed access & export audit — who viewed or exported a driver's records is itself hash-chained; an owner viewing records seals an entry. One-tap cutoff ends a departed driver's access.
📍Location privacy rules — the company sees location on duty / on trip only. Raw GPS breadcrumbs auto-delete after 30 days; sealed trip records remain.
💵Money-movement step-ups — when conversion and cash-out activate: fresh verification for large amounts, velocity checks, and review holds, all shown plainly.

The Settings sheet (top right) mirrors the full app's Security Center with sample values. An independent penetration test is required before real money moves — stated plainly, not buried.

Privacy & data — Security Center

🔐 App PINON · SAMPLE
Stored as a salted PBKDF2-SHA-256 hash (120,000 rounds) — never as the PIN itself. 5 wrong tries locks the app for 15 minutes, and changing the PIN requires the current one.
🚪 Sign out & getting back inTOP BAR
Sign out sits in the top bar beside the menu; one confirm tap signs out this device. Getting back in always takes a real credential — app PIN, Face ID / fingerprint, or the full sign-in under “Sign in with a different account.” There is no one-tap back-in, and the signed-out screen shows no account name or email. Sign-out-everywhere and the active-sessions screen still live here in the Security Center.
🧾 EIN on fileENCRYPTED
AES-256-GCM encrypted at rest, and only ever shown masked: ••-••••1234. Reveal is owner-only, behind the PIN, and every reveal is logged and sealed into the audit chain.
💳 PaymentsIDEMPOTENT
Every charge carries a unique key, so a retried or double-tapped payment can never charge twice. Card numbers are never stored or touched by the app — they go only to the licensed payment processor at go-live, so there's no card data here to steal.
⛓ On-chain anchoring & escrowOFF
Off until a separate go-live approval. Records are sealed in the app's hash chain today; no keys live in the app and nothing moves on-chain in this build.
🧱 Wallet wallENFORCED
Company screens, logs, and every export carry zero wallet data — no setting changes that. The exports on the Money tab are built to prove it.
🔗 Hash chainINTACT
Chain head (sample): 8f2ce7a1… · PIN, payment, and security events seal into the same chain as trips and loads, and integrity is checked on open.
🌳 Daily Merkle rootANCHORING OFF
Each day's sealed records roll up into a single Merkle root (sample): 4d7a…c201. At go-live, that one root is what gets anchored on-chain — a single fingerprint proving the whole day, without exposing any single record. Anchoring stays OFF until the separate go-live approval.

Preview: this panel mirrors the full app's Security Center with sample values — no real PIN, EIN, or payment exists in this copy, and nothing here can be changed for real.
